Subject: Runbook rehearsal: lateral-fallback verification + smoke acceptance

Hi Lisa / ACME ops team —

Thanks again for locking in the private deployment window next week. Before the production cutover we want to run a focused rehearsal of the runbook that specifically validates:

- Lateral fallback path (traffic steering to backup region)
- KV-cache priming and prefix warmup sanity
- ACL checks and firewall rules (east-west)
- Minimal smoke acceptance (key probes + tokenized generation sanity)

I attached the editable runbook (runbook-v3.2.pdf) and a checklist (smoke-checklist.csv). Can you confirm the team who will be on the bridge and their phone/pager? We propose:

- Tue 2026-11-04 14:00-15:00 PT 

Agenda (30 min runbook walk, 30 min practical rehearsal):
1) Walk through handoff and cutover triggers
2) Execute lateral-fallback trigger (dry-run)
3) Run smoke checklist probes (observability + generation)
4) Validate rollback/rollforward acceptance criteria

If that slot works, we'll bring Marissa (ops lead), Rishi (networking), and Monica (SRE) on the bridge.

Quick ask: can you confirm your ATC and firewall rule snapshot so we can mirror during rehearsal?

Thanks — Naomi

--
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Runbook rehearsal: lateral-fallback verification + smoke acceptance

Naomi —

Thanks for the note. Tue 11/4 14:00 PT works for our team. I'll be on the bridge; Ben (senior infra) and Priya (network lead) will join as well. Our on-call pager: +1 (213) 555-9987.

We can share the firewall snapshot — attaching our exported ruleset (we'll post the actual export to the shared Drive link you provided).

One item: when you run the lateral-fallback dry-run, can you ensure the test doesn't flip public traffic? We only want control-plane routing changes and mirrored traffic probes. Also please confirm whether your KV priming script will use traffic replay or synthetic prefixes — we want to understand network egress requirements.

Best,
Lisa

lisa.perez@acmecloud.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Perez <lisa.perez@acmecloud.com>, acme-devops@example-acme.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-03T12:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Runbook rehearsal: lateral-fallback verification + smoke acceptance

Thanks Lisa — perfect. Short answers:

- We will NOT flip production public traffic. The rehearsal uses control-plane policy changes in the staging routing table and mirrored probes from the test harness.
- KV priming will use synthetic prefixes generated by the priming script; we can toggle to replay if you prefer (we generally recommend synthetic to avoid PII).

I've updated the runbook to call out the mirror-only lateral-fallback procedure (see page 6) and added a note on egress ports for the priming job (443 only; TCP keepalive). Attaching network-fallback-diagram.png for visibility.

On the bridge: Naomi (host), Marissa (ops lead), Rishi (networking), Monica (SRE). We'll publish the meeting invite in 30min and include dial-in + doc links.

Naomi

--
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Lisa Perez <lisa.perez@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T13:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Runbook rehearsal: lateral-fallback verification + smoke acceptance

Quick network note before the rehearsal:

- Confirmed ACL snapshot from ACME received and validated.
- Lateral-fallback dry-run will be executed by toggling the routing policy on the control plane only; we will not apply BGP withdraws to peers.
- During the dry-run I'll also validate that the backup region's NAT gateway has the correct SNAT ranges so the priming probes see consistent source IPs (this matters for your WAF allowlist).
- If we hit an unexpected ACL rejection, the playbook instructs an immediate rollback to the previous policy and an ops sync — estimated time-to-recover for policy rollback is ~4 minutes if the rollback path is clear.

I'll post a short watchlist in the doc before the call.

-rishi

Rishi Malhotra
Network Lead | Redwood Inference

Subject: Post-rehearsal readout: green with two low-risk action items

Thanks everyone for joining the rehearsal. Short readout from today's runbook playback (14:00-14:55 PT):

Summary:
- Lateral-fallback dry-run executed; control-plane policy toggled, traffic mirrored — NO public flip observed.
- KV priming completed using synthetic prefixes; average priming latency 1.8 ms per token on test harness.
- Smoke checklist passed (all probes healthy).

Observed issues / action items (low risk):
1) ACME WAF allowlist: Ben to add the backup-region SNAT range to the allowlist. (owner: Ben / ACME; due: 2026-11-06)
2) Runbook clarity: update step 3 to explicitly call out the metric name for token-error-rate so SREs use the right alert. (owner: Naomi/Marissa; due: 2026-11-05)

Attachments from rehearsal: runbook-v3.2.pdf (updated), smoke-checklist.csv (results populated), network-fallback-diagram.png

Next steps:
- ACME to confirm WAF allowlist update by end of day 11/06.
- Redwood to submit final cutover safety checklist and a short rollback playnote after ACME confirmation.

Thanks again — rehearsal was smooth. I'll open the HubSpot activity and mark this stage as "Pre-cutover rehearsal completed".

Best,
Naomi
